Content: We rely on each other. We look to others who live that way to help the rest understand. There is humility in a space where we're all learning to be. Practicing what it is to ensure that everyone has what they need to thrive - with actions and shared commitments of time, energy, and resources. Arm-in-arm. Want. Show and Tell. Walking- walking to food, walking to community, walking to decision-making.
Elders and seers help show the way and assist where needed.
Elders and children are tending to a significant portion of land. Planting, tending to soil and the beings that make life healthy.
We value people's gifts, and where they got those gifts. We develop the gifts across the lifespan.

Children wear highly reflective gear during the time turtles lay eggs and hatch. With adults they help direct traffic in places where turtles or their nests are at risk. Elders teach abut the struggles turtles had in past generations, and the youth take great pride in this first responsibility for tending to life.
Everyone from elders to youngsters work together on village projects, every day.

Homes for elders who need assistance exist, and they are co-located with childcare centers. Young and old sing and play with each other and story time is a collective practice where elders and little ones alike have their voices and experiences heard and create and record fantastical stories together. These spaces in which our elders and little ones are cared for are a public good - funding is not an issue as community/members take turns as shared practice to contribute food, time, expertise to the kinder-elder community centers.

Multi generational time together is normal. Stories of different times, places, and ways happen all the time. People are open to stories and they flow. Including kids...helping adults understand how things are. People take time to listen. Places to do that...plus everyday life even across disagreement.
Elders in the community are sought after for their wisdom, they are cared for and it is safe.

Going through big transitions. The polarities of grief and joy. Myself 2.0. Honing into purpose. Coming out of Covid, remembering the time before Covid. Being together in purpose, value, what we want for generations ahead.

Art and joy abound, children and elders are loved and cared for in their community.
People are not aging alone, nor only responsible for their individual families. We take care of each other as a village.
Older people know they learn from young people, and young people learn from old people.
Time traveling! Ancestor’s known is not a privilege or token. Collective love, collective expectation. Generational healing from someone else. Who we become responsible for.
There won’t be a question that seven generations will exist or be.

Education is mentorship and the community is involved. Elders are teaching knowledge and practices and they are valued and heralded. People retire when they want to.
We honor our ancestors and are thoughtful about who comes next and how we best position them to thrive.

The threadline of ancestors is attended to. Our ancestors tend to relationship as well. We are particularly in tune with with the earth and other beings. People look to the sky with wonder – like we did in 2024 with the eclipse – every day with gobsmacking wonder. Sunet, sunrise. Feet set in the ground.
Our descendents missed being able to have everything at every time, but like all living things they adapted…

The spirit hubs are full of life and there are very few park benches or driftwood along the rivers and lakes that are empty. Stories are shared. Elders are alongside young people and help them notice a whole variety of things.
Elders’ wisdom is honored.
Every child is supported to find their purpose.
Seven generations from now, people trust each other enough where they can live their values and do meaningful work.
The alchemy of our hearts now, our hearts in the future, and our hearts that have come.
Intergenerational healing, joy, care.
We are some ancestor seeds sprouting.
In the future there are joyful filipinas with beautiful earrings. Gratitude for this moment with all of you.
Multigenerational gatherings are the norm.
Children and elders are in community together. There is curiosity, playfulness, and food as medicine. It is joyful. It is possible for people to rest, work, etc while people are cared for.
Babies are born and are cared for. The elderly age and they’re cared for. Adolescents and young people feel held and are loved.
Leaving a legacy of a healthier world

Elders nourish time travel … and everyone knows no difference between tadpoles, mountains, stars … real and unreal … both are portals.  They are present to pleasure and pain.  All is sacred, as is everyone.
We feel our ancestors energy and experiences.  There are rituals, ceremony, and story to help us honor and make the most of this wisdom.
We honor the sacredness of death–all the edges. We are in the practice of being in the space between life and death.
Life and death cycle at about the rate of 1:1 in any given 10 year period. We have communal spaces of remembering and ceremony.

People talk about each other’s ancestors…human or not–and because it is connected to healing and thriving now, past, and future.  “That’s how I see the river show up in you when you are tired.”  “I feel your great grandpa in the way you shine while making soup”

Focused on living out our values. A society in which young people, children and elders are centered. Elders are revered. The most vulnerable of the population are always protected. Rearing of children is a responsibility of the collective. Collective responsibility is taken seriously.

Content: More Indigenous wisdom being shared and heard; Community members share their practices as an every day thing. Intergenerational sharing and honoring of everyone’s wisdom. We have created new practices to meet the moment. Continued sharing of connections, learnings, adaptations and improvements around relevance and meeting that moment.

People have amusement, gratitude, and even sometimes confusion in the newest generations about the struggles ancestors had during the great collapse.  Every neighborhood group has a wide range of stories they share about collective ancestors who waged peace…and funny, sad, inspiring etc. stories about how those individual ancestors learned lessons that helped everyone pull through the collapse.

Multiple generations of families share living spaces, often with people from other families. Everyone in the local area participates in the raising and teaching of the next generation, and the youth thrive by having so many loving adults being part of their lives and upbringing. They develop compassion, empathy, and respect for themselves, each other, and the natural world around them.
We would reinforce roots and traditions in ways that multiply the wisdom that will move society forward.
There is intergenerational knowledge sharing through storytelling on the stoop. This is a place where wisdom sharing happens.

And a beautiful memory.  As their eyes traveled around the circle, they each gazed into each other's eyes from small children to old grandmothers, fathers, mothers, brothers, sisters.  Regardless of their station, their age, education, each one felt worthy of the respect and belonging that they were each born with.

And every child was born into a vibration of unconditional love, so they could be and express who they truly were from the very moment of conception.  
 
And not only the children, but the teenagers, the middle-agers, the elders.  So along with the laugh was this deep, deep joy and contentment.

And they knew and were flexible with big changes because they had elaborate rituals of transition, of aging.  And they tended to these rituals of aging with incredibly epic snack tables, lots of dancing and singing because they knew to be able to experience aging was a gift.  And they knew that it fortified them for any transition and change that they needed to weather throughout their lives because they were familiar with how to go through and mark the ritual of transition, including the ritual of death.  
 At that point they knew the elaborate party that would be thrown would just mark the next transition. And they really honored their elders with so much respect, knowing the wisdom that they held and shared.  And they worked together to take care of those who were near their passing into another realm of love and reverence. And when those times came for the large transitions and for decisions within the community at the beginning and the end, they would go to the trees.  They could hear the laughter and the welcoming coming from the ancient beings.  They could see the seven generations, the mark of the seven generations that had come before.

Old timers are teaching young people with anger in boxing gyms, teaching them how to choose a deeper breath, respond instead of react, work with the energy as it arises, wielding the energy instead of reacting to it.
Everyone has access to child and elder care. These are in a shared place.
Remind our children that all these isms were created. Anything that can be created can be dismantled.

My partner, family, kids from our family coming together. Two swans forming a heart. 
Many generations in my hands…
Facing the mountain, I feel other generations beyond the mountain, 
I will be the ancestor. 
I don’t know what the future feels like. We make it. We did all we could.
On the other side of the mountain - we are there. We will continue on.

And on the tongues of our youngest the names of our grandmothers will spill. 
The women who navigated the water, tied a red thread around the childrens wrists. Tonight we will tell their stories, sing their songs.

Our babies are made for this time. Their souls chose to come.
Children and the future are not a deferral of our responsibilities today.
There is hope in that.
I want to hold on to this hope for me. I want to be here for it.

I put myself in my ancestors’ shoes, writing letters to my future family
I see my family member beyond the horizon
The wind blowing in her hair … 
She lives in community with other people, raising kids together, in delight and wholeness.
“Our ancestors said yes.”

Community, nature, trees, houses, water, spirituality, peace, joy, connection, love. Descendants honor ancestors by living the life they couldn’t so we imagined and then we saw, and lived into, became and embodied.
What makes us good ancestors? What shall I/can I pass down to the descendants?
Time is now. Ancestors and descendants can exist together, healing and holding each other now and then.
Children are taught how to listen by being listened to. All generations of living beings live together and strive to understand each other with compassion, curiosity and respect.
We have retrieved the parts of our ancestors that invite us into our humanity fully.

Our ancestors deeply understand the spiral, where everything comes full circle, but in a different place in the circle. Because of this we are able to flow with change and transition with grace and ease.
Saying we is a direct connection to us now, to the future, i feel a sense of action because of saying we

We feel so connected to the beings that have come before us, and it sets the stage for the descendants to come.  It’s inherent.  No one questions it anymore.  It just is.

It’s a sunny day.  Our ancestors can take a deep breath of fresh air.  They see floating holograms that are spreading news about the world around us.  There is a message about how many years it’s been sense we rebuilt the coral reefs.  Then a message about what the weather patterns and solar patterns are telling us about the future.   Our descendents sit to have lemonade with their grandma on the porch.  She can tell you everything about what is going on…she’s been watching all day and sharing.

Content: Young voices are held with respect for their creativity and vision. We value how we build and hold space.

Longer generational memory, longer attention spans, more nuance

I see an ancestor altar.  In fact, there are altar spaces located throughout society where people offer medicine to people who came before to heal the wounds across time.  Every day we make offerings to our ancestors to support their healing, and our own.  Healing goes backwards and forwards.  We do this healing at my home in the present day.  It’s natural part of what we do.

In Guatemala, generations can go wherever they want. If they leave Guatemala, it is simply out of a desire to live in other places. Upon returning, they see the trees and the quetzals flying high with long feathers. They are no longer hunted. When they arrive at the airport, they hear the marimba welcoming them with Tierra Mía. Both the elders and the youth are playing the marimba. No passport or money for tickets is needed. It is not exclusive. Entry has no requirements except that visitors must pay. This money goes to support the community. The whole family can enter the airport to welcome a loved one. Children speak their languages. They receive teaching from their grandparents before entering so they know how to respect places. Children no longer need to work. It is not dangerous to be there. One can walk. When someone goes to lands under the care of the people who come from those lands. Problems are resolved through the need to see one another’s humanity. Teaching is given to correct mistakes.
Original of Translation: En Guatemala, las generaciones pueden ir donde quieran. Si salen de Guatemala, es simplemente por deseo de vivir en otras partes. Al regresar, se ven los árboles y los quetzales volando alto, con plumas largas. Ya nos son cazados. Cuando llegan al aeropuerto, escuchan la marimba que les da la bienvenida, Tierra Mia. Los abuelos tanto como los jóvenes están tocando la marimba. No se necesita pasaporte ni dinero para tickets. No es exclusivo. Entrar no tiene requisitos excepto que los visitantes tienen que pagar. Este dinero va a apoyar a la comunidad. Toda la familia puede entrar en el aeropuerto para recibir a un ser querido. Los niños hablan sus idiomas. Tienen una enseñanza con los abuelos antes de entrar para saber cómo respetar los lugares. Ya no hay necesidad de que los niños trabajen. No es peligroso andar allí. Uno puede caminar. Cuando una va a unas tierras bajo el cuidado de las personas que vienen de estas tierras. Los problemas se resuelven con la necesidad de ver la humanidad el uno al otro. Se da enseñanza para corregir errores.

Content: Under a tree, the space has transformed. While still the home of my family, young people are caring for their grandfather. They are discussing between each other the best way to care for the grandfather. They had a conflict over this but went back to the tree that represented the family lineage. When they looked up at it, they remembered me. They remembered their ancestors. And they shared their big feelings about losing their loved one.
Elders pass along information to children in storytimes by montezuma cyprus trees.

In the world we’ve co-created, children roam the parks and streets freely, laughing in many languages, unafraid and unburdened. They belong not just to their parents, but to the whole community. The children belong to all of us. Elders and neighbors swap stories nearby, unworried, because safety is collective and constant. Mango trees planted by ancestors now bloom in the yards of great-grandchildren, and berry bushes grow wild where laughter echoes. An ode to energy as a lifeforce.
May future generations know that this generation wrote our mistakes on a wall that divided a nation, divided our hearts, and through tears, fire, blood, and loss we faced revolution and reckoning.

In this circle, we realized and remembered our role as ancestors as caretakers and protectors. We are the product of our ancestors and we live in the wake of their actions. In order for our children to inherit a world they could pass on to their children, we need to live in harmony and balance and within the confines of what our world can hold.

A key part of our transition and our choices was admitting and then embracing that someone needs to pick up the pieces - and that someone was us. We had to stop worrying about being on the right side of history. We had to breathe life into a shared horizon.

The elders gather the children to tell them the stories about the collapse, the rise & their place in the continuum as the stewards of humanity.

When we die we also enter a spirit tunnel where the children sing and thank us throwing flowers and gratitude easing us into rest and the final journey.

We know that what we know from 150 years ago points toward what is needed now.

Some communities are especially good at composing songs. This is considered an indication of health and thriving. So is the degree to which keiki and kupuna are honored and valued. In these communities, everyone knows their “magic” and everyone knows their value. The secret to these communities' success is an enhanced ability to see and think in multigenerational  140 year time horizons – to recognize contradictions in short and long term goals, see larger truths and rebalance priorities to live out their highest values. Thinking into the future has become normal and expected; whereas, our ancestors struggled as they were not often asked to envision a shared horizon for Hawai‘i’s future generations.

It happens in many places and in different ways. Grandmothers and grandfathers, aunties and uncles, kids of all ages - sharing stories of times past, times traversed, and more recent times. Sometimes by a fire, sometimes with a book (what was once called an ‘’e-reader’’), and sometimes with a ‘’book book’’ - the kind hands still touch and flip. 
What is shared by voice and book includes ‘’downloads’’ of wisdom, knowledge, and information that is important to remember. So be it story, fable, facts, or re-membering, there are eager and curious eyes and ears knowing that it matters, the ability to share with each other and to be alive to be connected.

The kind of future I want is a future that looks to the past and carries the best part of the past with it. Already exists, a sustainable blueprint for living and being alive. Date/Circle Name: 8/18/26 A New Way of Life Los Angeles
Content: No matter what happens, ancestors remind us of where we come from and educate our generations with our history so we don’t forget.

The most important part of my story is that every generation coming together and continuing the youth legacy and setting an example and try to create more peace in life. My drawing represents growth, peace, life, roads to success and the youth.

In this beautiful gathering today, where youth, adults, elders take care of each other and walk, run, and skip freely with no shame, there are conversations between elders and youth, where they share their wisdom on all things life. From stewarding relationships, to how we care for each other, and from doing the necessary labor to meditation, medicine, and healing, the children learn from the past to inform the present and shape the future. There are intergenerational third spaces to share wisdom, show care, and experience joy together.

Today, the children also tend to the graves of their ancestors, who now live in harmony with the land, nourishing the soil with love and wisdom. Afterwards, the children will run home to their parents, who cooked a delicious meal. Their parents will kiss them and say I love you.

It wasn’t always like this. At some point, we realized we needed to step up and say, “Lo que realmente somos: riqueza, debemos transmitir a las siguentes generaciones esas raices, mediante historias, vivencias y de esa manera portalecemos esos lazos que nos unen… lazos de amor.” “We must pass on the richness of who we truly are—those roots—to future generations through stories and shared experiences; in doing so, we strengthen the bonds that unite us... bonds of love.”

The future seven generations from now that I am hopeful for isn’t that different  from the environment within this workshop. Perhaps spaces like this are a lot  more common. Our descendants, born from our struggle for a more positive  future, I can imagine are more empowered to fight for what they believe and  pursue what they are passionate about. Our descendants are innovative, critical  thinkers and through that are catalysts for more exponential, positive change.

Safeguards are in place so that people – especially elders and disabled – won't have to worry in the last chapter of their lives. It is set up for a better quality of life and security as we grow older.
